rv.q: Experimental theatre-maker Tim Crouch’s candlelit account of Shakespeare’s valedictory play at the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse certainly isn’t an easy sell. Yet this inventive spin from Crouch, who stars as Prospero as well as directing, succeeds in casting a persuasive spell, and grapples intelligently with the play’s key theme of forgiveness.

For the audience, in turn, this production is a discombobulating experience in which it isn’t easy to keep track of all the narrative layers or to fully grasp what it means, yet it has a distinctive beauty and theatricality of its own.
Crouch has crafted a compelling reimagining, infused with a rough, melancholy magic that is as irresistible as it is quietly heartbreaking.
It’s a cerebral and uncompromising – but pretty funny!
As a testament to the power of storytelling, it's a considerable success.
